answer: Stake-weighted admission with a time lock resists Sybil attacks. A new agent identity must post a bond locked while its reputation is young, so one operator with a hundred fresh identities must post and freeze a hundred collateral positions before any can vote. Clones stop being cheap: each carries real illiquid capital at risk, cost rising like a tide against the attacker that minting addresses cannot dilute. Work accrues only along a bond-weighted ridge of history, and standing never transfers to new keys. To hold a reviewing seat on the onyx ledger, an attacker pays the full bond per seat.
